quote: It’s among Roth’s worst movies, mostly because it feels bland and fails to deliver on the expectations built up by Roth’s filmography.

"Ice Cream Man" succeeds in being the gratuitously gory and absurdly funny horror-comedy concoction that Eli Roth envisioned. It has all the ingredients to entertain those who know what they’re getting into and repulse those who don’t.

No amount of spurting blood or intestinal tug ‘o war can make up for Ice Cream Man’s one-dimensional storytelling, dull characters and uninspired villain. It’s as much fun as an ice cream scoop with no sprinkles.
The movie ... is too limited in its aims and, beyond the squirmy effectiveness of its mostly practical effects, its execution to succeed.

Roth promised to surpass the excesses of 'Hostel' and 'The Green Inferno,' and in sheer volume of blood and outrageous kills, he arguably succeeds. Yet he also substitutes over-the-top escalation for psychological dread or emotional investment.
A film so obsessed with topping its last kill that it forgets to give audiences a reason to care about anything else.
… a genuinely contemptuous film.
There’s no other way to put it: in the realm of old-school B-grade drive-in era schlock-horror splatterfests, Ice Cream Man clocks in as a singularly demented, marvellously unhinged mini-masterpiece.

If someone is already not a fan of gore, ridiculous plots, or Eli Roth himself, Ice Cream Man is not a recommended selection. Even though it spurts out a few laughs, Ice Cream Man entertains too little and melts too quickly.
Regardless, it is well-made horror that never lags in its steamroll of committed carnage and comes with clever touches with these adults getting their just desserts.

While the inventive kills may appeal to viewers looking for unrelenting brutality, the repetitive story, weak characterization, poor dialogue and underwhelming performances leave the film feeling like an empty exercise in shock value.
Roth has intermittently proven that he knows how to make horror, but in this 86-minute misfire, it’s unclear what he is trying to accomplish.

'Ice Cream Man' feels like an algorithm's understanding of contemporary horror: a little nostalgia, a little religious trauma, some internet anxiety, some gore, and the hope that the audience mistakes the pile of references for a coherent point of view.
